newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Coast Guard seeks to rescue cargo ship.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Coast Guard seeks to rescue cargo ship.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard said on Thursday it had launched a rescue of a disabled cargo ship carrying oil that was drifting near the Aleutian island of Atka.
The 830-foot Liberian-flagged cargo vessel Baneasa lost power on Wednesday and was drifting toward Atka at about two knots, the Coast Guard said.
The ship had a crew of about 30 on board, plus 4,200 barrels of heavy fuel oil and 800 barrels of diesel fuel, but no cargo, the Coast Guard said.

The agency, along with state officials and the ship's owner, set up its oil-spill response system. It flew its California-based Pacific Area Strike Team to Alaska and flew oil-spill cleanup equipment to the nearby island of Adak.

By midday Thursday, it appeared that a Coast Guard cutter would be able to reach the cargo ship and tow it to safety before any collision occurred, officials said. Also in the area was another tug ship, prepared to take on escort duties.
"We're going to plan for the worst, but hope for the best," said Coast Guard Petty Officer Todd Taylor, a spokesman for the agency.
Atka is about 1,200 miles (1,900 km) southwest of Anchorage.
The Baneasa, homeported in Monrovia, Liberia, is operated by Torvald Kalveness and Co. of Norway, Taylor said.
The ship was adrift with its rudder stuck in the starboard position, he said.
